_meta.notes: Matric: 2025 NSC results announced by the Minister of Basic Education on 2026-01-12: national pass rate 88% (reported as 'about 0.7 pp' above 2024's 87.3%; the one-decimal value 88.0 is therefore inferred, not separately confirmed); bachelor passes 46% (48% in 2024); >656,000 passed; >900,000 full-time and part-time candidates wrote. Source used is the government news agency report of the DBE announcement — the DBE report itself was not retrieved; confirm the exact decimal, the pass-rate denominator, and the bachelor-pass base against the DBE NSC report. Provincial matric rates in provinces.json remain the 2024 values (only KZN 90.6% and Free State 89.33% were found for 2025, so a partial update was not made). Literacy is Census 2022 (unchanged). Higher-education enrolment (public universities, 2023) is unchanged: no newer DHET 'Statistics on Post-School Education and Training' edition was found, and the 2023 value was not re-verified. Do NOT run the World Bank updater script for this dataset (it overwrites verified values with annual modelled figures); update manually from the official Stats SA/SARB/DBE release — see antigravity-instructions.md.
_meta.public_notes: Matric: 2025 National Senior Certificate results, announced by the Minister of Basic Education on 12 January 2026. The national pass rate was reported as 88%, and the one-decimal value shown is inferred from that report. Provincial matric rates are still the 2024 values. Literacy is from Census 2022. Higher-education enrolment is for public universities in 2023.

statistics.title: National Matric Pass Rate
statistics.description: The national senior certificate (matric) pass rate for the 2025 academic year was 88%, the highest on record and about 0.7 percentage points above 2024 (87.3%). Over 656,000 candidates passed; more than 900,000 full-time and part-time candidates wrote, the largest cohort ever. Bachelor's passes (university entrance) were 46% of passes, down from 48% in 2024, although a record 345,000+ candidates qualified for degree study. All nine provinces were above 80%; KwaZulu-Natal was highest at 90.6%.

statistics.title: Adult Literacy Rate (20+)
statistics.description: Proportion of adults aged 20 and older who can read and write, as recorded in the 2022 National Census. This represents significant improvement from 85.0% in 2011. The next census is expected in 2032.

statistics.title: Higher Education Enrolment
statistics.description: Total headcount enrolments at public universities for the 2023 academic year, across 26 public higher education institutions. This excludes TVET colleges and private higher education institutions.
